concept.name: Hybrid Vector & Keyword Search

relationships.description: Connects Hybrid Vector & Keyword Search to llm prompt engineering in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: Hybrid vector search combines sparse lexical scoring (BM25) with dense semantic embeddings (HNSW/IVF) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and optional cross-encoder reranking to achieve high recall on both exact identifiers and conceptual queries.
spark.keyTakeaway: Dense vectors alone miss exact SKUs, error codes, and proper nouns, while BM25 misses synonyms; run both in parallel, fuse with RRF (k=60), and cross-encoder rerank only the top 20–50 candidates.

concept.whyItMatters: Pure semantic (dense vector) search excels at paraphrased intent ('how to fix memory leak in JVM') but routinely fails on exact tokens like `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`, `SKU-4920B`, or `RFC 9113`, where a single character difference shouldn't be blurred into nearby embeddings. Conversely, BM25 nails exact keywords and rare acronyms but returns zero results when a user searches 'car' for a doc titled 'automobile'. Hybrid search captures both signals in <30–50 ms and dramatically cuts RAG hallucinations.
whenToUse: Enterprise RAG, documentation search, and support knowledge bases where users mix natural-language questions with exact product codes, API names, or error strings.
E-commerce catalog search combining conceptual intent ('warm waterproof jacket for winter hiking') with exact brand/model/SKU filters.
Code and log search where exact symbol names (`NullPointerException`, `max_hint_window_in_ms`) coexist with semantic descriptions.
whenNotToUse: Pure exact-match lookups (primary key, UUID, order ID) where a B-tree or inverted index alone is faster, deterministic, and 10x cheaper.
Tiny datasets (<5,000 short records) where brute-force cosine similarity or SQLite FTS5 fits in memory and avoids HNSW index complexity.
Ultra-low-latency (<5 ms) autocomplete where running a transformer embedding model on the query path blows the latency budget.
keyPoints: Sparse retrieval (BM25 / SPLADE) scores exact term frequency and inverse document frequency (IDF), excelling at rare tokens, SKUs, and acronyms.

Dense retrieval embeds queries and chunks into fixed vectors (e.g., 768–1536 dims via `text-embedding-3-small` or `bge-m3`) indexed in HNSW graphs for ~10 ms approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) lookup.

Reciprocal Rank Fusion (`RRF_score(d) = sum(1 / (k + rank_i(d)))`, typically `k = 60`) merges uncalibrated BM25 scores and cosine similarities using rank positions alone—no brittle score normalization required.

Metadata pre-filtering (e.g., `tenant_id = 'acme' AND year >= 2025`) must be integrated into the HNSW traversal (single-stage filtered ANN in Qdrant/Milvus/Elasticsearch) to avoid empty top-k results from post-filtering.
Two-stage retrieval sends the top 50–100 RRF candidates to a cross-encoder reranker (`bge-reranker-v2-m3` or Cohere Rerank) to jointly attend over `(query, doc)` tokens, boosting NDCG@10 by 8–18%.

examples.title: Developer Docs & Error-Code RAG Assistant
examples.scenario: A cloud platform indexes 180,000 API doc chunks in Qdrant (1024-dim dense HNSW + BM25 sparse vectors). A developer queries: `why does webhook return ERR_HMAC_MISMATCH_401`.
examples.outcome: Dense search alone ranks generic OAuth/401 guides above the exact HMAC page because the rare error token wasn't well-represented in the embedding model's pretraining. BM25 ranks the exact `ERR_HMAC_MISMATCH_401` section #1; RRF (`k=60`) + cross-encoder reranking places it at rank #1 with 0.94 relevance, eliminating support tickets.

examples.title: E-Commerce Catalog Search with Tenant & Stock Pre-Filtering
examples.scenario: A marketplace with 4M SKUs in Milvus / OpenSearch runs hybrid search for `ergonomic mesh chair under 300` with `in_stock = true AND price <= 300`.
examples.outcome: Single-stage filtered HNSW + BM25 evaluates the stock/price bitset during graph traversal, returning 40 valid in-stock matches in 24 ms (vs. post-filtering returning only 3 results out of top-40).

tradeOffs.pro: Combining BM25 + HNSW + cross-encoder reranking consistently outperforms either retriever alone across BEIR benchmarks.
tradeOffs.con: Requires maintaining both an inverted index and a vector HNSW graph (higher RAM: ~4–6 GB per 1M 1024-dim float32 vectors without quantization) plus GPU/CPU budget for reranking.

tradeOffs.factor: RRF (Rank-Based) vs. Linear Score Fusion (alpha * dense + (1-alpha) * sparse)
tradeOffs.pro: RRF needs zero score calibration and is resilient to BM25's unbounded `[0, inf)` scale vs. cosine's `[-1, 1]`.
tradeOffs.con: Discards score magnitude gaps (e.g., a 0.99 exact match vs. a 0.51 weak match look identical if both are rank #1).

tradeOffs.pro: Full cross-attention between query and document tokens resolves subtle negation and multi-hop phrasing.
tradeOffs.con: Adds 40–150 ms per query on GPU (or 200+ ms on CPU) for top-50 candidates, unsuitable for <10 ms typeahead.

failureModes.name: Post-Filtering Recall Collapse
failureModes.description: Running unconstrained top-20 ANN first and then filtering by `tenant_id = 'acme'` (which owns 1% of rows) leaves 0–1 results after filtering.
failureModes.mitigation: Use engines with single-stage filtered HNSW (bitset evaluation inside graph traversal) or partition indexes by high-selectivity tenant keys.

failureModes.name: Naïve Score Addition Without Normalization
failureModes.description: Summing raw BM25 scores (e.g., 14.7) directly with cosine similarity (0.82) causes BM25 to dominate 18:1, silently disabling semantic search.
failureModes.mitigation: Use Reciprocal Rank Fusion (`k=60`) or min-max/z-score normalization per query before weighted combination.

failureModes.name: Chunk Boundary Context Loss
failureModes.description: Splitting documents at fixed 500-character boundaries cuts headings from paragraphs or splits tables, causing both BM25 and embeddings to miss the relationship.
failureModes.mitigation: Use structure-aware chunking (Markdown/HTML headers, 10–15% overlap) and prepend document title/section breadcrumbs to each chunk before embedding.

failureModes.name: Aggressive Quantization Recall Drop
failureModes.description: Compressing 1536-dim float32 vectors straight to 1-bit binary quantization without oversampling + rescoring drops recall@10 by 10–20% on nuanced queries.
failureModes.mitigation: Use int8 scalar quantization (minimal recall loss, 4x RAM savings) or oversample top-100 binary candidates and rescore against full-precision vectors on disk.

commonMistakes: Adding raw BM25 and cosine similarity scores without RRF or normalization.
Applying metadata filters *after* top-k ANN retrieval instead of inside the HNSW traversal.
Sending 500+ candidates to a cross-encoder reranker, blowing the p99 latency budget.
Using the same embedding model on queries and documents without required instruction prefixes (e.g., `query: ` vs. `passage: ` for E5/BGE models).
Storing unindexed raw float32 vectors at scale without int8/PQ quantization or disk-backed mmap, causing OOMs.

sections.content:
## The idea

Modern search faces a fundamental split: **lexical retrieval (BM25)** matches exact character tokens weighted by rarity (IDF), while **dense vector retrieval (HNSW)** maps text into continuous geometric space so semantically similar phrases cluster together.

Neither is sufficient alone. Dense encoders compress a 300-token chunk into a single vector, inevitably blurring exact identifiers like `CVE-2023-44487`, `x-amz-request-id`, or `SKU-9910`. Meanwhile, BM25 is blind to synonyms (`latency spike` vs. `p99 tail regression`) and paraphrased intent.

**Hybrid vector search** executes both retrievers in parallel over the same corpus (with shared metadata filters), merges the two ranked lists via **Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)**, and optionally passes the top 20–50 candidates through a **cross-encoder reranker** that reads query and document together for final precision.

## Concrete walkthrough

Trace a query `"kafka consumer lag spike after rebalance"` against a 500,000-chunk engineering runbook index in Qdrant/OpenSearch:

1. **Query Preparation**: The gateway generates a 1024-dim dense vector `v_q` (12 ms) and tokenizes the query for BM25 (`kafka`, `consumer`, `lag`, `spike`, `rebalance`). Both branches carry the pre-filter `org_id = 'payments'`.
2. **Parallel Retrieval**:
   - **Dense HNSW branch** traverses the multi-layer proximity graph with the `org_id` bitset filter and returns top-50 chunks (`14 ms`), surfacing conceptually relevant articles on *cooperative sticky assignor* and *partition revocation*.
   - **BM25 branch** queries the inverted index (`8 ms`) and returns top-50 chunks matching the exact rare terms `rebalance` and `lag`.
3. **RRF Fusion (`k = 60`)**: A chunk ranked #2 in Dense (`1/62 = 0.0161`) and #1 in BM25 (`1/61 = 0.0164`) scores `0.0325`, beating a chunk ranked #1 only in Dense (`0.0164`).
4. **Cross-Encoder Reranking**: The top-30 fused chunks are scored in a single GPU batch by `bge-reranker-v2-m3` (`38 ms`), promoting the exact runbook covering `max.poll.interval.ms` rebalance storms to rank #1. Total search latency: **~72 ms**.

sections.eyebrow: 03 / Score fusion math: RRF vs. linear combination
sections.content:
## Score fusion math: RRF vs. linear combination

**Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF)** is the industry default because it requires zero tuning across heterogeneous score distributions:

`RRF(d) = 1 / (k + rank_dense(d)) + 1 / (k + rank_sparse(d))`

With `k = 60`, rank #1 contributes `0.01639`, rank #10 contributes `0.01429`, and rank #50 contributes `0.00909`. Documents appearing in *both* lists naturally jump ahead of single-signal matches. When domain tuning is required (e.g., favoring exact SKU matches 70/30), use **min-max normalized linear combination** (`0.7 * norm_bm25 + 0.3 * norm_dense`) or **Distribution-Based Score Fusion (DBSF)**, which normalizes each list using `mean ± 3 * stddev`.

## Retrieval stage trade-offs

| Stage | Signal Type | Typical Latency (500K chunks) | Strengths | Weaknesses |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **BM25 / Inverted** | Exact tokens + IDF | 5–12 ms | SKUs, error codes, rare proper nouns | Blind to synonyms & paraphrasing |
| **Dense HNSW (int8)** | Bi-encoder cosine | 8–20 ms | Synonyms, cross-lingual, intent | Blurs exact IDs & negations |
| **RRF Fusion (k=60)** | Rank positions | <1 ms | Calibration-free, boosts dual hits | Ignores raw confidence gaps |
| **Cross-Encoder** | Full token cross-attention | 35–120 ms (top-30) | Highest NDCG@10 precision | Too slow for >100 candidates |

## Failure modes

- **Post-filtering empty results**: Filtering *after* top-k ANN fails whenever selectivity is <5%. Always use single-stage filtered HNSW.
- **Uncalibrated score addition**: Adding raw BM25 (`0..25+`) to cosine (`0..1`) silently breaks semantic recall.
- **Missing model prefixes**: Asymmetric models (`e5-large`, `bge`) degrade sharply if `query:` / `passage:` prefixes are omitted.
- **Stale index / delete drift**: Updating a document without deleting its old chunks leaves phantom results in both BM25 and HNSW.

## Memory & quantization sizing

At 1 million 1024-dim vectors:
- **Float32 HNSW (`M=16`)**: `1M * 1024 * 4 bytes = 4.1 GB` raw vectors + `~0.5 GB` graph edges (`~4.6 GB` RAM).
- **Int8 Scalar Quantization**: Cuts vector RAM 4x to `~1.0 GB` (+ `0.5 GB` graph) with <1% recall@10 drop.
- **Binary Quantization + Oversample**: Cuts RAM 32x (`~128 MB`), provided you fetch top-100 and rescore against disk-backed float32/int8 vectors.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Run BM25 and dense HNSW in parallel with single-stage metadata pre-filtering.
- [ ] Start with RRF (`k=60`) before attempting weighted linear fusion.
- [ ] Cap cross-encoder reranking to top 20–50 fused candidates to hold p99 under 100 ms.
- [ ] Use structure-aware chunking (300–600 tokens) with title/heading breadcrumbs prepended.
- [ ] Apply int8 scalar quantization once vector RAM exceeds 50% of node memory.
- [ ] Evaluate recall@20 and NDCG@10 on a golden query set covering both exact IDs and paraphrased questions.

interviewProblems.title: Hybrid Vector & Keyword Search
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on Hybrid Vector & Keyword Search. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: Hybrid vector search combines sparse lexical scoring (BM25) with dense semantic embeddings (HNSW/IVF) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) and optional cross-encoder reranking to achieve high recall on both exact identifiers and conceptual queries.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: BM25 Inverted Index applies the primary invariant and coordinates with RRF + Cross-Encoder.

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, RRF + Cross-Encoder experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Use engines with single-stage filtered HNSW (bitset evaluation inside graph traversal) or partition indexes by high-selectivity tenant keys.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Dense vectors alone miss exact SKUs, error codes, and proper nouns, while BM25 misses synonyms; run both in parallel, fuse with RRF (k=60), and cross-encoder rerank only the top 20–50 candidates.
Avoid trap: Adding raw BM25 and cosine similarity scores without RRF or normalization.
Avoid trap: Applying metadata filters *after* top-k ANN retrieval instead of inside the HNSW traversal.
When to reach for it: Enterprise RAG, documentation search, and support knowledge bases where users mix natural-language questions with exact product codes, API names, or error strings.
When to reach for it: E-commerce catalog search combining conceptual intent ('warm waterproof jacket for winter hiking') with exact brand/model/SKU filters.

putItTogether.title: Putting Hybrid Vector Search Together
putItTogether.summary: Dense vectors alone miss exact SKUs, error codes, and proper nouns, while BM25 misses synonyms; run both in parallel, fuse with RRF (k=60), and cross-encoder rerank only the top 20–50 candidates.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Hybrid Vector Search before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Dense search alone ranks generic OAuth/401 guides above the exact HMAC page because the rare error token wasn't well-represented in the embedding model's pretraining. BM25 ranks the exact `ERR_HMAC_MISMATCH_401` section #1; RRF (`k=60`) + cross-encoder reranking places it at rank #1 with 0.94 relevance, eliminating support tickets.
